title: Cool-flame extinction during n-alkane droplet combustion in microgravity
summary: Preprint (CSSCI 2014) of the 2015 Combustion and Flame paper: n-heptane, n-octane and n-decane droplets in O2/N2/CO2 and O2/He/N2 at 0.5-1 atm, 14-25% O2. All three alkanes show hot-flame radiative extinction followed by quasi-steady cool-flame burning, with cool-flame K slightly below hot-flame K. In O2/N2 the cool-flame extinction diameter scales as [O2]^(-3/4); across diluents and pressures D_ce^2/K_c correlates with [O2]^(-3/2), as an NTC-crossover argument predicts.

items.claim: Hot/cool K for n-decane and n-octane with He substitution as in the record.
items.quote: The burning rate constants K (=dD2/dt) corresponding to the first and second stage combustion were found to be 0.41 and 0.33 mm2/s respectively.

items.claim: In O2/N2, cool-flame extinction diameters of heptane, octane and decane scale with ambient O2 molar concentration to the power -3/4.
items.quote: The cool flame extinction diameters vary as oxygen molar concentration to the power -3/4 for oxygen/nitrogen mixture.

items.claim: With CO2 or He replacing N2 and at different pressures, the residence time at extinction D_ce^2/K_c correlates with [O2] at the theoretical slope -3/2.
items.quote: Remarkably the data are reasonably well correlated, considering the number of variables involved in the experiments, and, within the appreciable scatter, the results are in agreement with the theoretical slope of -3/2.

items.claim: Cool-flame burning rates are slightly lower than hot-flame rates.
items.quote: The cool flame burning rates are slightly lower compared to the hot flame rates.

notes: Read the NTRS preprint, not the paywalled journal version. Typo in the paper: R383 is given as '14%O2 and 96%N2' (sums to 110%). The three heptane cases quoted (D0 3.91, 3.48, 2.49 mm at 1 atm) do not appear in the PSI-69 table by initial diameter, so they are probably later (FLEX-2 era) tests. For PSI-39 (CFI) this is precursor work: the -3/2 correlation is the one cited in the CFI presentations. Also listed under PSI-39, PSI-69; read once. items.quote: during this stage, there is substantial leakage of n-heptane and O2 through the flame, and very little production of CO2 with no soot in the mechanism. The fuel leakage has been suggested to be the source of the observed vapour cloud that forms after flame extinction.

items.claim: Second stage of quasi-steady burning supported by low-temperature chemistry after radiative extinction.

title: Dynamic Differential Image Circle Diameter Measurement Precision Assessment: Application to Burning Droplets
summary: Rasul, Avedisian, Xu, Hicks, Reeves (IEEE TPAMI 2022): automated droplet-diameter measurement with per-measurement precision for the FLEX-2 surrogate-fuel image set: 278 experiments on 11 fuel types (13 tethered, 11 fully occluded by soot), droplets 1.17-3.81 mm, 98% success, +/-0.2 pixel precision with limited occlusion.

items.claim: The FLEX-2 surrogate-fuel image set comprises 278 experiments on 11 fuel types: decane, decane/propylbenzene 25/75, 50/50, 75/25, heptane, heptane/iso-octane 50/50, heptane/toluene 50/50, iso-octane, n-octane, propylbenzene and toluene; 13 were tethered and 11 fully soot-occluded.
items.quote: The FLEX-2 experiments on surrogate fuels comprised 278 individual experiments (Table 1) for 11 different fuel types.

items.claim: Automated diameter measurement succeeded for 98% of free-droplet runs, with +/-0.2 pixel precision when soot occlusion was limited (image ~30 mm across 1024 pixels).
items.quote: In cases of limited occlusion, a measurement precision of ±0.2 pixels for the FLEX-2 dataset was achieved.

items.claim: The PSI-68 experimental table lists 8 fuels (iso-octane, n-octane, n-heptane, n-decane, ethanol, propanol/glycerol 95/5 and 80/20, heptane/iso-octane 50/50) and droplets 1.5-5 mm, whereas the flown surrogate-fuel set includes toluene, propylbenzene, decane/propylbenzene and heptane/toluene (not in the table) and droplets of 1.17-3.81 mm.
items.quote: The actual diameter of the droplet varies from 1.17 mm to 3.81 mm.

notes: Accepted manuscript on OSTI read in full; Table 1 read from the page image. DOI found by the reviewer, not given in the PSI record: 10.1109/tpami.2022.3170926.

title: Interpretation of Backlit Droplet Images from ISS Droplet Combustion Experiments
summary: Yu and Shaw (2014): Fourier-optics analysis of FLEX/FLEX-2 backlit droplet images for non- or lightly-sooting droplets; diffraction at the droplet edge, partial coherence and background variation bias diameter measurements; an iterative edge-finding algorithm is proposed.

items.claim: Diffraction at the droplet edge can cause significant errors in droplet sizes measured from the ISS backlit images; partial coherence and background variations add further error.
items.quote: It was found that light diffraction at the droplet edge can contribute significantly to errors in droplet size measurements.

notes: Open access (Sciendo) read in full. Method paper; no new combustion results. Not added to the records (the record already gives the ±50 um droplet-size uncertainty from the NASA report). Also listed under PSI-69; read once.
